newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China to act soon on held Shell worker -oil source.
newsitem.headline: China to act soon on held Shell worker -oil source.

text.p: Beijing will soon come to a resolution over the detention of a Royal Dutch/Shell employee and her counterpart from a mainland oil company, a Chinese oil industry source said on Tuesday.
"I think the case would see a resolution very soon," the Chinese source, who declined to be named, told Reuters by telephone. "It would be done according to (Chinese) legal procedures."
Shell and China National Offshore Oil Corp (CNOOC) are involved in a US$6 billion joint venture refinery and ethylene complex together with other minor Chinese shareholders.
A mainland Chinese Shell employee and her CNOOC counterpart were arrested in March for what was later disclosed by Chinese sources as passing of state secrets.
But a Shell spokesman in Hong Kong said the company had not been informed of any new developments.

"We know nothing more about it...we understand it's to do with economic information," the spokesman said. "We're also as confident as we can be that there's no suggestion of corruption or bribery or any of these kind of things."

Chinese officials have repeatedly dismissed speculation that the multi-billion dollar project would be affected by the detentions. They have also said any alleged misconduct concerned the two detained employees and had nothing to do with the companies they represented.

A Chinese official involved in the project said last week that Beijing would soon give its long-awaited approval, possibly before end-1996, although many details of the deal would still need to be ironed out.
The complex in Huizhou in southern Guangdong province will house an eight million tonne per year refinery and 450,000 tonne per year ethylene plant. It is slated to come onstream after 2000.

If successful, it would be the second joint venture refinery involving foreign participation in China after the 100,000 barrel per day refinery in Dalian in the north. France's Total holds 20 percent of that facilty along with various Chinese partners.
